cards.explanation: The answer is a gentle lamb led to slaughter, friends. Jeremiah, the prophet, says, “…I was like a gentle lamb led to slaughter…” A lamb just trotting along, no clue what's coming. I think that's a tender thing to say about yourself.

The answer is True. Jeremiah says it plainly: “I did not know that they had plotted against me…” He was walking around with no idea. Then the LORD informed him, so he knew. Finding out what people have planned behind your back is a heavy thing.

The answer is False, friends. Jeremiah says to the LORD, “…for to You I have committed my cause.” He's putting it in the LORD's hands. He asks to see the LORD's vengeance, and he never says he'll take care of the plotters himself.

The answer is vengeance. Jeremiah says, “…let me see Your vengeance upon them…” He's talking to the LORD of Hosts, who judges righteously and examines the heart and mind. And remember, he's committed his cause to Him.

The answer is prophesy in the name of the LORD, friends. The people of Anathoth say, “You must not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or you will die by our hand.” They're seeking his life over it. I think that's one of the hardest things a person could hear, especially from his own hometown (Jeremiah 1:1).

The answer is that He will punish them. The LORD of Hosts says it Himself: “I will punish them.” Then He says what that will look like. Notice He's answering the people who were seeking Jeremiah's life.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says, “There will be no remnant…” He'll bring disaster on the people of Anathoth in the year of their punishment. It's a heavy line, so I'll just let it sit there.

The answer is wicked. That's the question Jeremiah brings: “Why does the way of the wicked prosper?” He even says he wishes to contend with the LORD about His judgments. And he starts by saying, “Righteous are You, O LORD…” I like that he talks straight to the LORD.
The answer is False, friends. Jeremiah says, “You are ever on their lips, but far from their hearts.” So the LORD's name is always in their mouths. Their hearts are somewhere else.

The answer is that they're far from the LORD. Jeremiah says, “You are ever on their lips, but far from their hearts.” The words say one thing and the hearts say another. Nice talk and a far away heart don't match.

The answer is to haul them off like sheep for slaughter, friends. Jeremiah says, “Drag away the wicked like sheep to the slaughter…” He also asks the LORD to set them apart for the day of carnage. He says this right after saying the LORD knows him, sees him and tests his heart toward Him.

The answer is True. Jeremiah says, “Because of the evil of its residents, the animals and birds have been swept away…” He also asks how long the land will mourn and the grass of every field be withered. The whole land is feeling it.

The answer is horses, friends. The words say, “…how can you compete with horses?” If men on foot already wore you out, horses are a whole other level. It's like getting winded on the walk to the mailbox and then signing up for a marathon. Bold move!

The answer is brothers. The words say, “…even they have betrayed you…” and they point to his own father's household. That one stings. It's the same kind of hurt we hear about with the people of Anathoth.

The answer is False, friends. The words say, “Do not trust them, though they speak well of you.” So even kind talk from his father's household isn't a reason to trust them. I think that's a lonely place for Jeremiah to be.
